learning_objectives: The learner will be able to explain what **tokens** and **tokenization** are, and why they are important for **LLMs**, **Context Windows**, cost, and **chunking**.

slides.title: Title Slide
slides.narration:
Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on
**Tokens** and **Tokenization**.
slides.image_prompt: Title slide with a graphic representing abstract data pieces forming words

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to
explain what **tokens** are.
And why they matter for **LLMs**.
You will also understand **Context Windows**, cost, and **chunking**.
slides.image_prompt: Learning objectives slide with bullet points

slides.title: Pre-requisites
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you should have
a basic understanding of **LLMs**.
And general **AI** concepts.
slides.image_prompt: Prerequisites slide with icons representing knowledge

slides.title: What are Tokens?
slides.narration:
Let's start with a fundamental concept.
**LLMs** do not read words like humans do.
They read something called **tokens**.
Think of **tokens** as the **LLM**'s building blocks for language.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of an **LLM** brain processing abstract blocks instead of human words

slides.title: Introducing the Tokenizer
slides.narration:
So, how do words become **tokens**?
A **Tokenizer** is the tool that does this.
It is like a special dictionary.
It splits raw text into smaller pieces.
These are sub-word pieces.
The **LLM** understands these pieces.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing text entering a machine labeled 'Tokenizer' and exiting as smaller, numbered blocks

slides.title: Tokenizer Examples
slides.narration:
Let's look at some examples.
A simple word like "The" might be one **token**.
But a complex word can be split.
For example, "**Tokenization**" might become three **tokens**:
**Token**, **iz**, **ation**.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison: 'The' as one block, 'Tokenization' broken into 'Token', 'iz', 'ation' blocks

slides.title: Why Tokens Matter
slides.narration:
Now you know what **tokens** are.
But why should you care?
**Tokens** are crucial for several reasons.
They affect how **LLMs** work.
They also impact performance and cost.
slides.image_prompt: Person scratching head, then lightbulb moment, with keywords: Context, Cost, Chunking

slides.title: Context Windows
slides.narration:
**LLMs** have a "short-term memory".
We call this a **Context Window**.
This memory is measured in a fixed number of **tokens**.
For example, it might be 8,192 **tokens**.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a limited window with small blocks (tokens) flowing through it, labeled 'Context Window'

slides.title: Context Window Limitations
slides.narration:
This **Context Window** is a hard limit.
It restricts how much information you can send.
This includes retrieved documents.
It also includes your **prompt**.
All this must fit within the **token** limit.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing a container with a fixed capacity, with 'documents' and 'prompt' blocks trying to fit inside

slides.title: Cost Implications
slides.narration:
**API** providers charge you per **token**.
More **tokens** mean higher costs.
This is important for budget management.
Especially for large-scale **AI** applications.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a hand dropping coins into a slot labeled 'API', with a counter showing 'Tokens = $$'

slides.title: Efficient RAG Systems
slides.narration:
An efficient **RAG** system can save money.
It uses fewer **tokens**.
For example, **GraphRAG** uses much fewer **tokens**.
This can make your **AI** system dramatically cheaper to run.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison: a large pile of tokens next to a smaller pile of tokens labeled 'GraphRAG', with a dollar sign icon

slides.title: Chunking and Tokens
slides.narration:
When we process documents, we often "**chunk**" them.
This means breaking them into smaller pieces.
These **chunks** are then processed by the **LLM**.
Understanding **tokens** helps us make effective **chunks**.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a long document being cut into smaller, manageable blocks labeled 'chunks', each containing a few tokens

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
With this, we come to the end of this tutorial.
Let us summarise.
We learned that **LLMs** read **tokens**, not words.
A **Tokenizer** splits text into **tokens**.
**Tokens** affect **Context Windows** and **API** costs.
They also influence how we **chunk** documents.
slides.image_prompt: Summary slide with key terms: Tokens, Tokenizer, Context Window, Cost, Chunking

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
As an assignment, please do the following.
Find an online **tokenizer** tool.
Type a long sentence into it.
Observe how different words are broken into **tokens**.
Then, try a complex word and see its **tokenization**.
